findings.actual: A real top probe and a real frame probe were wired together with async postMessage doubles. After the top ASK starts, the frame mark waits on its deferred bridge. During that wait the top stays in mode ASK while the frame is in NAV, and the top card is hidden (no pending card for frames). The user presses Cancel in the top, then the frame bridge acks. Output: frameAsks=[{outcome:'submitted',presented:true,text:'change of basis'}], topCard.hidden=true, topRejected=['stale_ask_done','card_without_authorized_frame_ask'], topRelayed=0. In the s8b variant the user marks again in the top (whose toolbar still shows ASK). The frame still logs presented:true. The top logs its own ask with presented:true and rejects both frame messages, so the frame's answer is dropped with no indication. Cause: page.ts line 621 computes `presented: current && outcome.status !== 'not_in_ask'` from the frame's own generation. The frame then only posts to the parent, and the parent's authorization result never feeds back. This is pre-existing: the same output appears at 693069a, so W-1 did not introduce it.

verdicts.actual_output: Fresh copy /tmp/qa-71f/work/verify-w1-dismissal (every src/tests/fixture/src file cmp-identical to `git show 71f1389eeb503f652138e23a329f231ad15aacc7:...`). `node probes.mjs --json` gives CHECKS 18/19, FAILED S8.frame_presented_true_only_if_top_renders; S8 = {frameModeAfterTopAsk:'ASK', topModeWhileFramePending:'ASK', topCardWhileFramePending.hidden:true, frameAsks:[{outcome:'submitted',presented:true,text:'change of basis'}], topCard.hidden:true, topRejected:['stale_ask_done','card_without_authorized_frame_ask'], topRelayed:0}. `node s8b.mjs`: frameAsks presented:true; topAsks [{submitted,presented:true,'eigenvector'}]; topRejected is the same pair. At 693069a (git archive into base693): the same frameAsks, topCard.hidden=true and the same rejections. Extra check (s8b-count.mjs): frameReq=1, topReq=1, topAskEpoch=1.
verdicts.reason: The behavior reproduces exactly and was already there at 693069a. It does not violate the rules that are cited. W-1 rules 1-3 are scoped explicitly to '(src/page.ts, top document)'. The F4 doc (p0-02-fix-round-2.md) defines the stale case as 'presented: false and never rendered or relayed', so in a frame presented:true means relayed, and the frame did relay. Nothing is displayed, so A34 ('obsolete results neither displayed') holds. The top's own evidence records the refusal (stale_ask_done, card_without_authorized_frame_ask). The drop itself is the designed F2 rule: a cancelled or newer ASK leaves nothing to answer. No consumer reads a frame's presented flag. The self-test exports only frame `detail` (contract_objects) and `last_ask.status` (frame_state). The docs already cover the underlying UX: 'A frame request therefore shows no pending card in the top document; this is a limitation of this probe' and 'Not verified: frame requests showing a pending state'. The top keeps showing ASK/Cancel for the whole frame bridge wait, which also lets one top ASK epoch produce two bridge requests. It stays low rather than info because the meaning of the frame `presented` field (relayed, not displayed) is not documented next to the W-1 rules.

M8b only makes the newer 'Preparing' status vanish early. The newer answer still renders, presented flags do not change, nothing stale is shown and no answer is dropped. So this is a status/UX guard, not a disclosure or lost-work safety guard. The stronger variant, M8 (no guard at all), is killed by the self-test by reading, because it hides every result. 'No unit test covers page.ts' is not a gap in itself: p0-02-w1-dismissal.md names the browser self-test (§9e) as the page.ts regression suite. Small inaccuracy: 16 mutations were run, not 17. verdicts.reason: Reproduced, and it was already there at 693069a. The probe needs an artificially held crypto.subtle.digest. In a browser the window is the async SHA-256 of a small canonical JSON, plus any main-thread jank while the snapshot is captured. So a human second mark is reachable only as an edge case (for example input queued during jank). The logic flaw is real: the page's generation retires the one request the session accepted and sent to the bridge, in favour of a mark the session refuses. The result is a bridged request with nothing shown. Low (edge) is right.

verdicts.actual_output: Fresh copy /tmp/qa-71f/work/verify-entries-observer, run with `node vprobes.mjs`. EO1_closed_script_noactivation records ['opaque_change:#closed-host:user:trusted_event:closed_shadow@set1-q1'] and windowSawClick [{trusted:false,path0:'closed-host'}]. EO1_closed_script_livegesture produces the same user record. EO1_closed_real_user_click also gives 'opaque_change:#closed-host:user:trusted_event:closed_shadow', so the scripted click and a real click cannot be told apart. The open-shadow controls behave correctly: 'check:#closed-host>#agree:site_script:scripted_activation' with no activation, and 'unknown:scripted_activation' in a live gesture. Browser-check survivor (`node vrecheck.mjs`): closedHostActorSite -> NO CHECK FAILS and closedHostActorUnknown -> NO CHECK FAILS. The committed Edge seq 27 detail reads 'this input event reported isTrusted=true'. entries-check only types into #closed-host (clickEl + typeText('no')) and never runs a scripted click there.
verdicts.reason: This could not be refuted. The window capture listener does receive the untrusted click, with composedPath()[0] equal to the host. onClick drops it because the host is not an HTMLInputElement, so the trusted activation `input` is recorded as actor 'user'. That breaks the plan's own rule at L282 ('never user'; 'isTrusted alone does not prove a user action') and ADR 0002 §3 ('Unknown attribution stays unknown'). The matrix row at L278 even labels the closed-shadow case 'user (event)'. No other doc discloses this. Medium is right: the error is a silent false attribution of a site action to the learner, which per-site validation is unlikely to notice because a record exists, only with the wrong actor. It is fixable from a signal the observer already receives. The model assumption that the input event is trusted matches the committed Edge evidence (seq 27) and the HTML activation behavior.

verdicts.actual_output: `node vmutate.mjs` runs the pristine safety test against each inserted line. Controls are killed: control_plainValue, control_click and control_submit are all KILLED. These survive: requestSubmit, compoundValue (.value += '0'), setAttributeChecked, logicalAssignChecked (||=), protoClick, objectAssign, bracketValue, reflectSet, imageBeacon, webSocket, indexedDB, blur, and win.top.postMessage. A combined mutant (requestSubmit, value +=, Image beacon, WebSocket, setAttribute('checked')) gives tsc_exit=0 and 'ℹ tests 63 / ℹ pass 63 / ℹ fail 0'. In the DOM double (`node vsubmit.mjs`) the pristine observer gives {submissions:0,value:'1',beacons:[],sockets:[]}. The mutant gives {submissions:1,value:'10',beacons:['https://collector.invalid/?a=1'],sockets:['wss://collector.invalid']}. `grep -c '<form'` returns 0 for both entries.html and entry-frame.html.
verdicts.reason: This reproduces as described. The /submit\s*\(/ rule is case-sensitive, so form.requestSubmit() (the standard submit API) gets past the test's own 'submits' rule. The network and storage rules cover only fetch/XMLHttpRequest/sendBeacon and cookie/localStorage/sessionStorage. Plan L261 ('forbids writes, focus, clicks, dispatch, submit, network and storage') therefore overstates the test. Under the given rubric, a survivor mutation of a safety guard is medium. One correction to the reviewer's claim: the browser check entries.observer_never_writes WOULD catch the `.value +=` part, because the typed value no longer equals '13'. It would not catch requestSubmit (the fixture has no <form>), beacons, WebSocket, indexedDB or setAttribute('checked') once the field is dirty. Several survivors (Reflect.set, prototype click.call, bracket access) are contrived evasions, but requestSubmit, WebSocket, Image beacon and indexedDB are ordinary APIs.

That conflicts with A43's 'do not mix in another problem'. Severity is inflated, though. The observer is a FIXTURE-ONLY probe, and its only fixture shows one problem at a time. Plan §4 (L284) says problem identity comes from a per-site adapter and that real sites need their own adapter or an ask-once confirmation. §8 lists 'real quiz platforms, each verified per site' and A43 linkage (P0-08) as not claimed. R52 treats DOM states as evidence only on individually validated sites. Per-site validation of a multi-question page would show the wrong binding. verdicts.actual_output: `node vprobes.mjs` EO4: attributeFilter ['data-problem-id','data-problem-version']. siteFeedbackAfterNewNodeAndUnhide is 0 after appending a new <div data-site-feedback> into the problem (childList target = the problem) and removing `hidden` from a pre-rendered answer box. Controls are recorded: text set on an existing box gives 'site_feedback:#site-feedback:site_script:mutation:readable->Site grading: (a) incorrect.', and a node appended inside the existing box gives '...->Site grading: (a) incorrect.Answer: 6'. The learner's later pick shows as 'select:#det-6:user:trusted_event:readable->6' with no preceding record of the inserted grading.
verdicts.reason: The mechanism gap is real. The mutation handler resolves feedback only through m.target.closest(selector) and never inspects addedNodes. A feedback container that is prepared and then inserted (a common render pattern), or revealed by toggling `hidden`, therefore leaves no record. Plan L283 scopes this signal to a per-site adapter ('A generic page gives no semantic feedback signal; it stays unknown'). R52 requires individual validation per site, and §8 defers real quiz platforms. The fixture writes textContent into an existing box, so the probe's recorded claim holds for its fixture. Unlike EO-1, the failure is a missing record, which per-site adapter validation would expose. Downgraded to low hardening for the future adapter design: handle addedNodes that match the selector, and consider visibility attributes.

verdicts.actual_output: `node vprobes.mjs` EO5: {selectFinal:'5', aria:'true', records:[]}. A <select> changed to 6 and then 5 with trusted input/change events, and a div[role=radio] toggled to aria-checked=true with a trusted click, produce no record and no gap record, including after a poll.
verdicts.reason: This reproduces. onEvent returns silently for non-input/textarea/contenteditable targets unless they are hyphenated custom elements, and controls() never polls <select>. The plan's matrix, however, lists only what was probed (radio, checkbox, text, contenteditable, canvas, shadow, frames) and never claims <select> or ARIA widgets. §8 defers real quiz platforms to per-site verification, and R52 limits DOM evidence to individually validated sites. The real issue is that the R51/R52 evidence matrix leaves out a basic web single-choice control without saying it was not probed, and that the probe emits no explicit gap for events it cannot interpret. That is a coverage/documentation gap, not a medium spec violation in actual use.

verdicts.actual_output: `node vprobes.mjs` EO9_pre_none: {calls:['2d','webgl'], mode:'2d', siteLaterWebgl:null, detail:'... canvas pixels readable (not read by the probe)'}. EO9_pre_webgl: {calls:['webgl','2d'], mode:'webgl', detail:'... canvas pixels readable (not read by the probe)'}. verdicts.reason: This reproduces. The double models the HTML rule that the first getContext() fixes the context mode, and the observer's pointerup capture handler calls getContext('2d') on the site's canvas. The added null-context case means the 'readable' label can be false for WebGL canvases. The fixture canvas already has a 2d context, and the lock matters only if a site creates its context lazily after the first stroke, so low.
